messages:
deploy-bot: Starting config-only deploy cfg-24681 at 2026-03-20T17:00Z. Changes: rate_limit 120r/s -> 90r/s, request_timeout_ms 12000 -> 10000, routing_policy 'prefer-cheap' weight 0.20 -> 0.10, batching.window_ms 8 -> 6. Canary: 2% traffic for 15m. No model or image changes. /deploy id=cfg-24681

alice: kicking off canary now, rolling to canary pool. I'll watch latency & error dashboards.

benji: oncall FYI. If p99 increases >200ms or error_rate >0.5% during canary, we rollback. Also monitor cost/token since rate reduction may increase unit cost.

carla_dev: just to confirm — this is config-only, no model pin changes, right? canary should still hit variant v1.2.3-quant.

alice: correct — no model bump. canary routed to same serving variant.

ezra_oncall: I'll be around for the window 17:10-17:40. ping me if any alerts.

ops-bot: Canary metrics update (5m): p50=36ms p95=105ms p99=280ms error_rate=0.12% cost_token_change=+2%

alice: p99 at 280ms — slightly above benji's 200ms soft threshold. We should avoid full ramp until we stabilize. Suggest reducing canary routing weight to 1% and shaving batching.window_ms to 4ms for canary only.

benji: +1 to hold. If we can get p99 back under 250ms with a small patch, continue. Otherwise rollback to previous config.

carla_dev: applying canary patch now: `deployctl update-config cfg-24681 --scope=canary --set routing.weight=0.01 --set batching.window_ms=4` will be live in ~30s. No downtime.

deploy-bot: Patch applied to canary at cfg-24681-p1. Observability links: https://dashboards.internal/redwood/cfg-24681/canary

ops-bot: Post-patch metrics (5m): p50=34ms p95=98ms p99=220ms error_rate=0.06% cost_token_change=+1%

alice: looks good. Recommend ramp to 20% for 30m. Ramp plan: 2% -> 5% -> 10% -> 20% with 5m checks, rollback conditions: p99 > 300ms or error_rate >0.5% for any step.

benji: documented rollback thresholds and rollback playbook updated in the ticket. Also note: revert routing weight to 0.20 if we rollback.

carla_dev: release-note draft: "config-only: reduced global rate_limit, tightened request timeout, lowered cheap-routing weight to reduce tail latency variance, reduced batching window for canary. No model or runtime image changes. Monitor latency and cost for 24h."

alice: proceeding with staged ramp. I'll post updates at each stage. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
